# Cross-Exchange Liquidity Commentary | 31 July 2026

US equity markets command the top tier, with Nasdaq 100 dominating on depth (0.0025% per $1M ILLIQ) and volume ($409.7M comparable), while NYSE offers the tightest spreads at 0.6578% AR despite slightly higher price impact at 0.0059% per $1M. The Western European cohort—Euronext, SIX Swiss, and Xetra—occupies a stable middle band with ILLIQ ranging from 0.0302% to 0.0534% per $1M, though all three show modest turnover ratios (0.15% to 0.65%) reflective of smaller constituent universes. Tokyo Stock Exchange stands as a regional outlier: its 2.8225% turnover ratio ranks second globally, yet its 0.0352% per $1M ILLIQ and 0.7615% AR spread place it only fourth, suggesting strong domestic participation masks wider effective spreads for foreign traders. Hong Kong and London occupy the lower-middle tier with comparable metrics around 0.08% per $1M ILLIQ, while Korea Exchange clearly lags, posting the worst ILLIQ at 0.1547% per $1M and substantially elevated spreads at 1.6274% AR, despite moderate turnover. This metric divergence—particularly Asia's strong turnover paired with wider microstructure costs—signals that volume concentration and pricing efficiency are decoupling in regional markets.
